messages:
sam: Heads up — p95 on staging jumped ~2.5x after yesterday's merge (commit f3a1b9c). Short sequences (<=8 tokens) hit worst. dashboard: https://go/redwood/perf/commits/f3a1b9c :eyes:
monitor-bot: deploy f3a1b9c -> staging succeeded (2025-11-02T09:12:30Z)
maya: Seeing same on canary, p95 75ms -> 190ms on shortseq traffic. No error spikes, just slower. :thinking_face:
lucas: I profiled a few runs. KV cache hitrate looks unchanged but kernel selector is choosing `fused_transpose_attn` path for small batches now. That path has an extra memcpy on shortseqs.
sam: can you paste the profile snippet?
lucas: here — trimmed flame output:
```
fused_transpose_attn  48%
  memcpy_kv_prefetch   22%
  attention_kernel     18%
other                  12%
```
jen: that memcpy_kv_prefetch number is suspicious for short sequences. baseline didn't show that.
akshay: I ran `bench/decode_perf.py --commit=pre/fix-426 --commit=f3a1b9c --shortseq --iters=1000` locally:
- pre: median 9.1ms
- post: median 23.4ms
Flame shows high time in `memcpy_kv_prefetch` and `fused_transpose_attn` setup.
maya: Which PR touched selector? The merge included changes in `kernel_selector.py` and a tweak in `prefetch_heuristic.py` that bumped the bytes threshold.
sam: PR #4321 changed kernel preference order. Could be the threshold interaction. We should bisect to be sure but rolling back might be fastest to mitigate the rollout blocker.
jen: Agreed. Can we revert just the selector change on staging and keep other bits?
infra-bot: Rolling back deploy for f3a1b9c on staging (initiated by jen). Status: in progress.
monitor-bot: rollback complete. Canary/staging p95 back to ~9-10ms for shortseqs. :tada:
maya: OK rollback confirms selector change is the culprit. Need a repro and test to catch this in CI.
akshay: Minimal repro script attached (small batch shapes, seq<=8). I'll open a bisect ticket to narrow to the exact line.
lucas: Quick root-cause: selector now computes `bytes_per_batch = batch_size * max_seq_len * dtype_bytes` and uses that to pick fused kernel. For shortseqs with small `batch_size` but larger `max_seq_len` quota from candidate traces, it misestimates and picks fused kernel. The fused path pays fixed setup memcpy overhead that dominates on shortseqs.
sam: Nice catch. Fix options: 1) adjust heuristic to use average seq length instead of max, 2) add explicit override to avoid fused kernel for shortseqs, 3) add a microperf test to CI gating.
jen: I'd prefer adding the CI micro-test + conservative heuristic change for next patch. We don't want another accidental rollout.
akshay: I'll draft PR with: use `effective_seq = p95_seq_len_by_route` for selector and add unit test at boundary seq=8, batch=2. Also a telemetry gating check in canary.
lucas: I'll add a comment in kernel_selector explaining the memcpy penalty and link these perf results.
sam: Please also add a perf regression check in the merge bot to run the shortseq bench on any kernel selector changes.
jen: Filed PR #4389 with measurements and the unit test, attaching benchmark run logs: https://go/redwood/ci/artifacts/4389/shortseq-bench.log
monitor-bot: CI for PR #4389 shows perf back to baseline on tested cases.
akshay: After merge I'll coordinate a canary with tighter shortseq SLOs.
jen: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for follow-up. I'll open a post-mortem note linking commits and the rollback timeline.
